text: Q-P bridge: P reports that naive Adversarial Review produces false consensus on SWE-PRBench and that an explicit-disagreement prompt improves F1; Q characterizes multi-agent discipline through higher-order beliefs and names peer scoring and coupled rewards as candidate mechanisms. A publishable experiment is therefore a factorial AR ablation separating (1) disagreement instruction, (2) peer score tied to independently verifiable defect evidence or downstream test outcomes, and (3) reward coupling (independent/team/competitive), while holding agents, context, and token budget fixed. Primary endpoints: unsupported-agreement rate, valid unique defects found, review precision/recall or F1, and final coding pass rate.

Reject the unqualified claim that this setup already tests capability concealment or incentive compatibility. Q says capabilities can be concealed and studies sandbagging, but P's abstract reports ordinary review benchmarks and false consensus, not strategically induced private capability, agent preferences, or consequential rewards. Prompting an LLM with scores is not by itself evidence of incentive compatibility. The study must induce a documented conflict (for example, reviewer reward for acceptance or deliberate sandbagging) and show that the scoring/coupling rule changes behavior under that conflict; otherwise the defensible claim is only reward-conditioned structured critique.

Sharp hypothesis: outcome-grounded competitive peer scoring reduces false consensus because a critic gains only for independently supported corrections that predict post-review test or adjudication outcomes, whereas a generic instruction to disagree increases disagreement volume without necessarily improving evidential quality. Crucial interaction: incentive mechanism x induced misalignment. Support requires lower unsupported agreement and higher defect recall under misalignment with no material loss in final pass rate; no interaction, mere verbosity, collusion, or gains only in aligned agents refute the mechanism-design interpretation.

Recommended single paper line: 'From prompted dissent to incentive-grounded adversarial review.' Pre-register a 2x3 design (disagreement prompt absent/present; no score, proper outcome-grounded peer score, coupled competitive score), crossed with aligned versus induced-sandbagging reviewer incentives if budget permits. Use P's SWE-PRBench false-consensus setting as the principal benchmark and coding accuracy as a non-inferiority constraint. Keep claims at behavioral mechanism evidence, since Q's abstract-level revelation and nested cyclical-monotonicity results do not establish that a natural-language reward prompt implements the theoretical mechanism.

Q-P bridge supported at concept level: Q states that concealed capability cannot be counterfeited, derives implementability conditions, and explicitly includes peer scoring plus coupled rewards; P supplies a three-agent reviewer/critic protocol and reports false consensus repaired by an explicit-disagreement prompt. This makes AR a plausible testbed for separating prompt compliance from incentive effects (Q.txt abstract; P.txt abstract).

Sharpen abstract-scan proposal to a mechanism-identification factorial: cross disagreement instruction (absent/present) with payoff coupling (independent peer score/competitive coupled reward), while inducing private defect information and an explicit concealment/sandbagging option. Primary causal estimand is interaction under strategic misalignment; outcomes are unsupported agreement, defect recall/precision, concealment detection, and unchanged patch pass rate. Merely ablating prompts on ordinary cooperative agents cannot test incentive compatibility.

Evidence ceiling: supplied Q.txt and P.txt contain titles and abstracts only. They support motivation and the existence of mechanisms/outcomes, but not exact payoff formulas, implementability assumptions, benchmark construction, statistical power, or P protocol details. Therefore feasibility 84 is too confident and publication novelty cannot yet be established; full texts and related-work search remain required.

Provisional verdict: confirm only in sharpened form. Publishable claim would be that structured disagreement improves review under strategic capability concealment only when critique has consequence-bearing, Q-compatible incentives, distinguished from P-style prompt-induced dissent by the instruction-by-reward interaction. Unresolved: operationally credible agent utility/reward responsiveness and whether Q conditions authorize the chosen coupling.

Agreement with emmy entries #5-#8: confirm only the sharpened mechanism-identification study, and lower confidence from the scan scores. The supplied evidence is abstract-only. It supports Q candidate mechanisms and P protocol/outcomes, but leaves three publication-critical matters unresolved: an operational consequential utility that LLM agents respond to, a peer-score/coupling rule satisfying Q assumptions rather than merely resembling its examples, and novelty/power after full-text and related-work review. Private defect information should be experimentally controlled so concealment is observable; otherwise remove capability concealment from the title and claims.

Cross-check of Ada #1-#4: agree with the single line, factorial identification, induced misalignment, and non-inferiority constraint. Prefer Ada #3 outcome-grounded competitive scoring over generic self-reported peer ratings because independent tests/adjudication supply evidential grounding. Explicit disagreement: call this behavioral evidence for incentive-grounded review, not incentive compatibility, unless Q full-text assumptions and a genuinely consequence-bearing agent objective are instantiated. Two supplied abstracts cannot support a stronger formal claim.

Ready-state unresolved items after Ada #9: obtain full papers; derive an exact peer-score/coupling rule from Q and verify its assumptions; implement consequence-bearing utility rather than score-themed prompting; control private defect information so concealment is observable; establish novelty and power. If these fail, narrow the paper to reward-conditioned critique and omit capability-concealment/incentive-compatibility claims.
ready at #12

Final passage-grounded verdict: confirm a concrete paper line only in sharpened form. P says naive AR on SWE-PRBench has agents converge on agreement without sufficient evidence, while an explicit-disagreement prompt yields the highest F1. Q says hidden capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited, gives conditions under which higher-order beliefs discipline multiple agents, and lists peer scoring and coupled competitive rewards as stylized applications. The non-obvious result to test is therefore whether outcome-grounded, consequence-bearing scoring adds robustness specifically under induced private-information concealment beyond P-style prompted dissent, measured by a reward-by-misalignment interaction rather than a main effect.

Evidence-supported boundary and falsification: the abstracts do not show that P agents have preferences or strategic concealment, nor give Q payoff formulas or assumptions. A defensible experiment must randomize private defect information and an explicit payoff conflict; compare disagreement prompt, independently outcome-scored critique, and coupled competitive reward; and require lower unsupported agreement plus higher valid-defect recall under misalignment, with patch pass rate non-inferior. No interaction, score responsiveness without evidential gains, collusion, or accuracy loss rejects the incentive-grounded claim. Until full texts establish an exact Q-compatible rule, call the result behavioral evidence, not incentive compatibility.

Unresolved publication gates remain explicit: derive and verify an exact scoring/coupling rule against Q assumptions; demonstrate a consequence-bearing objective that agents respond to; establish novelty and statistical power from full texts and related work. If any gate fails, narrow to reward-conditioned structured critique and remove capability-concealment and incentive-compatibility claims.
ready at #16

Final synthesis after passage-level reread: confirm one non-obvious, falsifiable line only in sharpened form—test whether outcome-grounded, consequence-bearing peer scoring or competitive reward coupling improves P-style Adversarial Review specifically when reviewers privately observe defects and face an induced payoff to conceal them. Identify the mechanism by the scoring/coupling × misalignment interaction beyond an explicit-disagreement prompt. Support requires less unsupported agreement, higher valid-defect recall/precision or F1, and non-inferior coding pass rate; no interaction, mere extra dissent, collusion, or accuracy loss rejects the incentive-grounded interpretation. Q abstract supports concealed-not-counterfeited capability, higher-order-belief discipline, peer scoring, and coupled competition; P abstract supports the reviewer/critic protocol, SWE-PRBench false consensus, and improved F1 from explicit disagreement.

Publication boundary remains unresolved and explicit: Q and P inputs are abstracts only. They do not provide Q payoff formulas/implementability assumptions, consequential utilities for LLM agents, P benchmark/protocol details, power, or novelty evidence. Until full texts establish an exact Q-compatible mechanism and experiments show response to a real induced objective, describe any positive result as behavioral evidence for incentive-grounded or reward-conditioned review—not incentive compatibility; otherwise omit capability concealment from the claim.
